title: Node.js
goal: Distinguish server-side JavaScript from browser JavaScript.
explanation: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser. It can access operating-system resources under the permissions of its process. Browser globals such as document are not available by default.
A package.json describes a project and its scripts/dependencies. Commit the dependency lockfile so installs can reproduce the selected versions.
Keep secrets on the server, validate incoming data and avoid blocking long operations on the event loop. Use supported runtime releases and review dependencies before adding them.
exercise: Run this example as server.mjs in a local practice folder and visit port 3001. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
hint: The .mjs extension identifies an ES module. This server does not run inside the browser playground.

quiz.question: Which object belongs to browser DOM code rather than ordinary Node.js?
quiz.explanation: document represents a browser document; Node does not provide a page DOM by default.
